identity.nameEn: Sri Lakshmi Narasimha Swamy Temple, Yadagirigutta
identity.spiritualSignificanceShort: Yadagirigutta is a hill shrine dedicated to Narasimha, the man-lion avatar of Vishnu, worshipped in a cave sanctum in five forms — Jwala, Yogananda, Ugra, Gandaberunda and Lakshmi Narasimha — said to have manifested for the penance of the sage Yadarishi. Popularly promoted as 'Telangana's own Tirupati', the temple was substantially rebuilt by the Telangana state government between 2016 and 2022 and is now among the state's most visited pilgrimage sites.

governance.establishedEra: Traditional origin in the Treta Yuga per the Skanda Purana; documented patronage under Nizam-era Hyderabad State in the early 20th century · Sanctum complex substantially reconstructed 2016–2022 by the Telangana state government
governance.managingAuthority: Endowments Department, Government of Telangana, through the Sri Lakshmi Narasimha Swamy Devasthanam Trust Board
governance.founderPatron: Modern reconstruction (2016–2022) undertaken by the Telangana government through the Yadadri Temple Development Authority (YTDA), initiated under then Chief Minister K. Chandrasekhar Rao

narrative.summaryIntro:
The Sri Lakshmi Narasimha Swamy Temple at Yadagirigutta, in the Yadadri Bhuvanagiri district of Telangana, is dedicated to Narasimha, the man-lion avatar of Vishnu, worshipped here in five forms said to have manifested for the sage Yadarishi. Known popularly as Yadadri and promoted as 'Telangana's own Tirupati', the hill shrine's cave sanctum houses the five Narasimha forms — Jwala, Yogananda, Ugra, Gandaberunda and Lakshmi Narasimha — beneath a golden Sudarshana Chakra said to be visible for several kilometres.

The temple most pilgrims visit today is largely the product of a 2016–2022 reconstruction carried out by the Telangana state government through the Yadadri Temple Development Authority (YTDA), distinct from the older hill-cave shrine it replaced. Inaugurated on 28 March 2022, the rebuilt complex is administered by the state Endowments Department and now draws tens of thousands of pilgrims daily.
narrative.documentedHistory:
Temple tradition, recorded on the temple's own website and traced to the Skanda Purana, holds that in the Treta Yuga the sage Yadarishi — son of Rishyasringa and Santa Devi — performed penance in a cave on this hill with the blessings of Hanuman. Narasimha, an avatar of Vishnu, is said to have appeared before him in five forms — Jwala Narasimha, Yogananda Narasimha, Ugra Narasimha, Gandaberunda Narasimha and Lakshmi Narasimha — giving the site its name, Pancha Narasimha Kshetram. This account is devotional tradition rather than a dated historical record. The temple's own history page also states that worship follows the Pancharatra Agama and credits Sri Vangeepuram Narasimhacharyulu, a former sthanacharya, with establishing the temple's puja procedures and composing the Yadagiri Suprabhatam.

Datable documentation of the temple's pre-20th-century history is limited in the sources reviewed for this record. Wikipedia states that the last Nizam of Hyderabad, Mir Osman Ali Khan, granted the temple Rs 82,825 during his rule, indicating the shrine was an established pilgrimage site under princely-state patronage before Indian independence; it also records that in February 2023 Princess Esra, former wife of the titular 8th Nizam, donated jewellery valued at about Rs 8 lakh to the temple.

The complex most visitors encounter today is the result of a large, state-government-led redevelopment distinct from the older hill shrine. Per Wikipedia, the Telangana government began rebuilding the temple in 2016 through the Yadadri Temple Development Authority (YTDA), headed by then Chief Minister K. Chandrasekhar Rao, and the reconstructed temple was inaugurated on 28 March 2022. Wikipedia reports a project cost of about Rs 1,800 crore, of which roughly Rs 300 crore was spent acquiring about 770 hectares (1,900 acres) of land, and states the temple's built footprint grew from about 0.81 hectares (2 acres) to about 6.5 hectares (16 acres), with a new bus stand built on a further 6.1 hectares (15 acres). The rebuilt complex is reported to use about 39 kg of gold and roughly 1,753 tonnes of silver to line gopurams and walls, with design credited to film-set designer Anand Sai, architect P. Madhusudhan and chief sthapathi Sundararajan Srinivasan, following silpa and Agama conventions executed in black granite in a style drawing on Kakatiya-period design. These figures are as reported by Wikipedia and were not independently corroborated against a primary YTDA or government financial account during this research, so they are treated as sourced rather than verified.
narrative.architectureStyle: Dravidian (the reconstructed complex draws on Kakatiya-period black-granite conventions, executed to Agama and silpa shastra principles)

visitingInfo.dressCode: No formal dress code is published; the temple's Do's and Don'ts page prohibits carrying mobile phones, caps, turbans and hats inside the temple premises.
visitingInfo.nearestRailStation: Raigiri station (renamed Yadadri, station code YADD, on the South Central Railway), approx. 5 km
visitingInfo.nearestBusStation: New TSRTC bus stand built at Yadagirigutta as part of the 2016–2022 redevelopment
visitingInfo.entryRules: General darshan is free; paid Special Entry (₹150) and Break Darshanam (₹300) ticketed categories are also offered, bookable online. The temple advises that darshan, seva and room-accommodation bookings be made online or by phone at least 48 hours in advance.
visitingInfo.officialContactNote: Devasthanam contact numbers: Reception/Protocol +91 8333994020, Online enquiry +91 8333994022 (9 AM–6 PM), Donations/Schemes +91 8333994025, Accommodation +91 8688322624; email eo-yadagirigutta@telangana.gov.in. Confirm same-day darshan and seva arrangements before travelling, as timings change on festival days.

openingHours.notes: The temple's own timings page states the temple is open from 3:30 AM to 9:45 PM, with darshan interrupted through the day by the sequence of daily poojas. The Government of India's Incredible India tourism portal gives a simplified two-block version (roughly 4:00 AM–4:00 PM and 4:00 PM–9:45 PM); the temple's own timings page is treated as authoritative here.

shrines.deityOrSubject: Five forms of Narasimha: Jwala, Yogananda, Ugra, Gandaberunda and Lakshmi Narasimha
shrines.locationDescription: Natural cave forming the sanctum sanctorum, described by Wikipedia as approximately 3.7 m high and 9.1 m long and by the temple's own site as sheltered beneath a large overhanging rock. A golden Sudarshana Chakra, about 3 ft by 3 ft, is set into the spire above it and is said to be visible from about 6 km away.
Subsidiary shrine to the right of the main temple entrance.
Bathing tank on the temple grounds, near which pilgrim housing was built as part of the 2016–2022 redevelopment.
Hall used for kalyanotsavam and related rituals within the rebuilt complex.
Seven gopurams with wooden roofing form part of the rebuilt temple complex.

poojas.description: The first service of the day, awakening the deity.
Early morning food offering to the deity.
Fire ritual (homam) dedicated to Sudarshana Narasimha.
Daily ceremonial wedding ritual of the deity.
Midday food offering to the deity.
Closing ritual of the day, after which the temple shuts.

festivals.significance: The temple's principal annual festival, with cultural programs including Harikathas, Bhajans, vocal recitals, Upanyasams and Bharatanatyam performances.
Marks the appearance of Narasimha; observed with Parayanams of the Ramayana, Mahabharata, Bhagavad Gita and the temple's own Kshetra Mahatyam.
Annual purificatory festival observed at the temple; the temple's festival page gives only the dates and no further description.
